description: The physics behind games and interactive simulations: kinematics and numerical integration, forces and Newton's laws, particles and springs, collision detection and response, rigid body dynamics with constraints, fluids and cloth, and keeping simulations stable and deterministic. Every method is derived, then implemented and visualised in a browser physics sandbox where students compare integrators, break simulations on purpose and tune them to run in real time on a phone.
modelledOn: Bridson, Fluid Simulation for Computer Graphics
outcomes: Model motion with vectors and kinematics and implement explicit, semi-implicit and higher-order numerical integrators.
Apply Newton's laws to compute forces such as gravity, drag, friction and springs and simulate particle systems.
Detect collisions and resolve them with impulses, restitution and friction for particles and rigid bodies.
Simulate rigid body dynamics in 2D and 3D, including rotation, inertia tensors, contacts and joint constraints.
Implement mass-spring cloth and particle-based fluids and explain the trade-offs between accuracy and speed.
Analyse the stability, energy behaviour and determinism of a simulation and design it for networked and replayable games.

units.title: Vectors, kinematics and the simulation loop
topics: Vector algebra for physics: dot and cross products, projections, normalisation and coordinate frames
Kinematics: position, velocity and acceleration; projectile motion and analytic solutions
The physics step inside the game loop: fixed time steps, accumulators and rendering interpolation
Units, scales and choosing world dimensions for a game; floating-point precision

units.title: Numerical integration
topics: Ordinary differential equations as the model of motion; initial value problems
Explicit Euler, semi-implicit (symplectic) Euler and velocity Verlet; local and global error
Runge-Kutta methods (RK2, RK4) and when the extra cost is worth it
Stability: stiff systems, the effect of step size, energy drift and damping
Implicit integration for stiff springs; position-based approaches as an alternative
Comparing integrators on an orbit and a spring and plotting energy over time

units.title: Forces and Newton's laws
topics: Newton's three laws, mass and momentum; force accumulation in an engine
Gravity, drag (linear and quadratic), buoyancy and friction (static and kinetic)
Force generators and registries; game-tuned forces versus physically accurate ones
Projectiles and vehicles: a thrown ball, a bicycle on a laterite road, an okada braking

units.title: Particles and springs
topics: Particle systems: emitters, lifetimes and effects such as smoke, fire, dust and rain
Hooke's law, damped springs and critical damping; bungees and anchored springs
Mass-spring networks: structural, shear and bending springs; soft bodies
Stiff springs and instability; fake springs and position constraints
Rods, cables and simple particle contact constraints
Building a rope bridge or a hanging chain in the sandbox

units.title: Collision detection for physics
topics: Broad phase and narrow phase: bounding volume hierarchies, grids and sweep and prune
Contact generation: sphere, box and plane tests, the separating axis theorem and contact manifolds
GJK and EPA for convex shapes; penetration depth and contact normals
Continuous collision detection and time of impact against tunnelling

units.title: Collision response
topics: Impulse-based response: relative velocity, coefficient of restitution and conservation of momentum
Friction impulses and the Coulomb friction cone
Resolving interpenetration: projection, Baumgarte stabilisation and slop
Resting contact, stacking and sleeping bodies
Simulating a game of marbles or oware seeds bouncing in a board

units.title: Rigid body dynamics
topics: Rotational kinematics: angular velocity, orientation as angles, matrices and quaternions
Torque, angular momentum, moment of inertia and the inertia tensor in world and body space
Integrating rigid bodies in 2D and 3D; normalising quaternions and avoiding drift
Contacts on rigid bodies: impulses at contact points and the effect on spin
Constraints and joints: distance, hinge, ball and socket; sequential impulse solvers and warm starting
Building a 2D rigid body engine with stacking boxes and a ragdoll

units.title: Fluids and cloth
topics: Cloth as a mass-spring system and with position-based dynamics; collisions and self-collision
Fluid models: Eulerian grids versus Lagrangian particles; the Navier-Stokes equations in outline
Smoothed particle hydrodynamics: kernels, density, pressure and viscosity
Grid-based smoke and water: advection, diffusion and pressure projection (stable fluids)
Height-field water and other cheap approximations for phones
Simulating a flag in the wind or kente cloth draped over a figure

units.title: Stability and determinism
topics: Sources of instability: large time steps, stiff constraints, mass ratios and accumulated error
Determinism: floating-point differences across devices, fixed-point arithmetic and fixed update order
Deterministic lockstep and rollback netcode for multiplayer; replays from recorded input
Performance: island partitioning, sleeping, solver iterations and budgets on low-end phones
Capstone: a physics-driven browser game with a documented, stable and deterministic simulation
